title: Hunter's Chicken Stew
subtitle: Braised chicken thighs with pancetta, mushrooms and tomatoes
excerpt: Hunter's chicken is a pub-classic braise of chicken thighs with pancetta, chestnut mushrooms, and tomatoes. It finishes in the oven under a blanket of melted cheddar. The smell alone is worth making it for.
sourceNotes: Hunter's chicken (pollo alla cacciatora in Italian) has British pub versions that add a cheddar and bacon topping. This recipe takes the braise from the Italian tradition and adds the British finishing touch.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the braise up to the cheese stage 2 days ahead. Reheat, top with cheese, and grill to finish.
recipe.temperatureNote: The oven is used to melt and brown the cheddar topping at the end.

content.text: If your stockpot is oven-safe, you can skip the baking tray and transfer straight from hob to oven. Grill on high for the last 3 minutes to get the cheddar bubbling.
Season the chicken. Brown in a hot dry stockpot for 4 minutes each side. Remove and set aside.
Add pancetta to the pot. Cook for 4 minutes until lightly crisp. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes. Add garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine vinegar. Let it bubble for 1 minute. Add tinned tomatoes, stock, and Worcestershire sauce.
Return the chicken to the pot. Simmer gently for 30 minutes with the lid on.
Transfer the chicken to a baking tray. Spoon over some sauce. Top with grated cheddar. Bake for 10 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden.
Serve with the remaining sauce spooned alongside.

items.symptom: Cheese topping is pale and unmelted.
items.cause: Oven temperature too low or time too short.
items.fix: Switch to grill for 3 minutes to brown quickly.

items.cause: Lid was on throughout and liquid did not reduce.
items.fix: Remove lid and simmer for 10 more minutes.
